name: John W. Goodall
role: Round-up foreman and Billings County commissioner
bio: John W. (Johnny) Goodall was a Little Missouri cattleman and round-up foreman. In April 1884 the stockmen recommended him as foreman of the round-up, and that spring he brought back 47 cow horses from the west, along with the Mexican rider Perfecto Fernandez; that winter he broke teams for the stage road. In April 1885 the Montana Stock-growers' Association named him to district the Little Missouri, and in April 1886 the Little Missouri River Stockgrowers' Association elected him foreman of the spring round-up. He married in August 1885, entered horses in Medora's Fourth of July races that year, and ran for Billings County commissioner on the March 1886 ticket; by July he sat on the board and chaired meetings pro tem. He was elected commissioner for Precinct Two in November 1886, and in December left for San Antonio, Texas, on business for the N. P. Refrigerator Car Co.
